meta.title: From a Brief to the Record

views.label: 1 · What was asked
views.note: A brief is whatever your product wants done. It is content; the runtime never interprets it.

views.label: 2 · What it may see
views.note: The catalogue is the registry narrowed by the ceiling in force, so a forbidden tool is not refused — it is invisible.

views.label: 3 · The plan
views.note: Tool calls become a Composition: Invoke, Await, Sequence, FanOut, Until. The plan is a value, not a script.

views.label: 4 · One governed step
views.note: The composition is compiled to a graph and each node is judged then run. The runtime never interprets the plan.

views.label: 5 · Three different exits
views.note: Information, a request to remember, and something that already happened. They are not the same kind of thing.

meta.subtitle: What becomes what, and the two very different ways anything leaves the runtime.

cards.title: What each box holds
items: Brief — what was asked, in your product's own words
Catalogue — the registry narrowed to what this run may see at all
Model — whatever thinks; it answers with text and tool calls
Composition — the plan as data: five step kinds, compiled to a graph
Governed step — the judged execution of one node of that graph
Then three exits, and the difference between them is the point of this drawing

cards.title: Two kinds of write, and only one is forbidden
items: Changing the world happens through a component whose effects are declared and judged
Changing your record happens only by proposing; your own gate decides
The runtime has no write path into any durable store — that is the whole of propose, never commit
The event stream is neither: it is information, and nothing an observer does can reach back in

cards.title: Why the plan is data and not code
items: A Composition is a value: it can be inspected, stored, compared and re-emitted
It is compiled to a graph and executed by the engine; the runtime does not interpret it
It is emitted as an event whenever it changes, so plan-versus-actual costs nothing

cards.title: What the model is allowed to see
items: The catalogue is filtered by the ceiling, so a forbidden tool is invisible rather than merely refused
Handles carry real values between steps, so a large result is never flattened into tokens
An act on the world leaves a receipt with its key, its exit and the authority it ran under
